title: Enterprise Frontend: React 19, SSE Streaming Hook & Interactive Citations
description: Build the enterprise React 19 + TypeScript frontend: custom SSE streaming hook with AbortController cancellation, interactive citation popovers, tool execution status badges, and human-in-the-loop action approval modals.

data.text: The Modern Streaming AI User Interface

Building a production user interface for an enterprise AI assistant presents challenges absent in standard CRUD applications. The frontend must parse fragmented Server-Sent Events (SSE) chunks on the fly, render streaming Markdown without layout thrashing, dynamically transform raw `[cite:UUID]` tags into interactive citation cards with document previews, show live tool-execution spinners, and intercept high-impact agent actions with modal approval dialogs.

data.caption: React 19 Streaming State Transitions with Tool Approval Intercept
data.code:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Submitting : User submits prompt
    Submitting --> StreamingTokens : SSE stream opens
    StreamingTokens --> StreamingTokens : Append delta tokens
    StreamingTokens --> AwaitingApproval : Backend emits ActionApprovalRequired event
    AwaitingApproval --> ActionApproved : User clicks 'Confirm & Execute'
    AwaitingApproval --> ActionRejected : User clicks 'Reject'
    ActionApproved --> StreamingTokens : Agent resumes tool execution
    ActionRejected --> StreamingTokens : Agent handles cancellation
    StreamingTokens --> Completed : Received [DONE] event
    StreamingTokens --> Aborted : User clicks 'Stop Generating'
    Completed --> Idle
    Aborted --> Idle

data.text: Production SSE Streaming Hook with AbortController
The custom `useStreamingChat` hook consumes the SSE endpoint using `fetch` with `ReadableStreamDefaultReader`. It manages token accumulation, error recovery, and immediate HTTP abort capability.

data.title: useStreamingChat Hook in TypeScript
data.content: This production hook manages streaming state, token accumulation, and instant cancellation using AbortController.

data.text: As the assistant streams text, inline markers like `[cite:3e8f4c21]` must not render as ugly plain text. A Markdown renderer regex plugin replaces citation tokens with clickable pills that open a flyout preview of the source passage.

data.title: Citation Badge and Drawer Component
data.content: Renders citation badges that open the source excerpt drawer with high contrast and accessibility compliance.

data.text: When an agent invokes a destructive tool (e.g. creating a purchase order, deleting a record), the backend emits an `ActionApprovalRequired` SSE event. The UI captures this event, suspends UI input, and renders an approval confirmation modal with diff visualization.

data.title: React 19 AI Frontend Quality Checklist
items: AbortController actively tied to 'Stop Generating' button to cancel network stream immediately
SSE stream reader handles line breaks and JSON token fragmentation without crashing
Citations rendered as interactive components with keyboard accessibility (tabbing and Enter keys)
Auto-scroll to bottom behavior respects user scroll-up (does not snap violently while user reads history)
Tool execution spinners provide clear feedback on what the agent is currently doing
Human-in-the-loop approval dialog clearly highlights consequences and parameters before executing

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: React 19 streaming UI delivers immediate visual feedback via custom SSE hooks.
AbortController guarantees control over runaway or unwanted token generation.
Interactive citation badges anchor LLM statements in verified source documents.
Next, we implement the end-to-end RAG ingestion worker and hybrid vector search.
data.takeaway: An enterprise AI frontend is more than a chat box: it is a mission control panel providing transparency, citation verification, and human oversight over autonomous agent tools.
